newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ alcohol tax rise in June "will hurt industry".
newsitem.headline: NZ alcohol tax rise in June "will hurt industry".

text.p: A government decision to raise excise tax on alcoholic drinks in June would further harm the hospitality industry, Hospitality Association chief executive Bruce Robertson said on Tuesday.

On April 28 cabinet decided excise tax would rise on June 1 by two percent under the government's six monthly consumer price inflation indexation regime. It estimated the change would raise about $10.2 million a year.
"Last year the consumer paid $500 million in tax and you'd think the government might give them a rest," Robertson said.
He said reductions in prices as a result of competition had not increased consumption.
"The per capita consumption has reduced, operators are getting unacceptable returns on their investment in the industry and price hikes, like the June 1 increase, add to the financial pain," he said.

Beer, Wine and Spirits Council executive director Hamish Riach, said the rise was at odds with the government's anti- inflationary economic policy and showed little regard for the impact on the economy or the consumer.
Customs Minister Neil Kirton was not immediately available for comment.
Kirton's spokesman, Michael Laws, said the decision would raise about $10.2 million a year.
"I don't understand what they are getting upset about. It happens every year," Laws said.

Customs Service director of corporate communications, Andy Anderton, said the impact would be an extra two cents on a jug of beer, three cents on a bottle of table wine and 32 cents on a 1125 ml bottle of whisky.
"It is up to the discretion of the government whether it will proceed on any or all (classes of alcoholic drinks). In this case it has decided to proceed on all," Anderton said.
